about: Arrests for the minor quality-of-life offenses the justice case flow models (disorderly conduct, drunkenness, liquor law violations, curfew and loitering violations, vagrancy), per 1,000 residents a year, by state, D.C. and territory, for 2024. This is the real recent level the outcome web's justice.low-level-arrests starts from (src/core2/data/outcome-web/outcome-web.json keptOutcomes holds the same per-place numbers; src/core2/justice-low-level.test.ts checks the two agree). Real rates check totals; they never decide whether one person is arrested.

source.publisher: FBI Crime Data Explorer, arrest data
source.offenseCodeList: The offense codes are the FBI Crime Data Explorer API's own arrest_offense list (https://cde.ucr.cjis.gov/LATEST/webapp/#/pages/docApi).
source.method: Each value is the sum of the 12 monthly arrest rates (arrests per 100,000 people the reporting agencies serve) of the five offenses, divided by 100 to read per 1,000 residents. This is the method the web's crime.violent base uses for the FBI's monthly rates. The rates cover the population of agencies that reported that month (minCoverage is the lowest monthly share of the state's population covered, across the five offenses).
source.classDefinition: Chalfin, Hansen, Weisburst and Williams (2022) call this group 'quality-of-life' arrests: 'lower-level “quality-of-life” offenses (including disorderly conduct, liquor violations, loitering, and drug possession)'. The game's class leaves drug possession out (it belongs with the drug laws, an owner question in the pull request) and keeps the owner's examples (disorderly conduct, loitering, public intoxication). Since 2021 the FBI collects arrests through NIBRS, and agencies that did not convert report fewer categories: a state whose agencies report no drunkenness arrests shows 0.0 for it here, which is how the source reads, not a measured zero.

national.note: The United States row of the same source: all reporting agencies together.

notReported.note: No arrest counts for these categories in the source for 2024 (American Samoa, the Northern Mariana Islands and the U.S. Virgin Islands return no months; Puerto Rico returns twelve months of zero for every category and for all arrests). The web starts each of them from the national value above, marked ESTIMATED, and never from zero.
